newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks ease on profit taking, Tokyo loss.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks ease on profit taking, Tokyo loss.

text.p: Thai stocks ended a four-day winning streak to close lower on Friday on profit taking partly induced by a sharp retreat of Japanese stocks, brokers said.
The SET index ended 2.72 points lower at 840.50 on moderate four billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index slipped 0.22 point to 63.09.
"Market sentiment was quite poor due to the decline on the Nikkei index. Investors sold stocks, mainly banks and finance, to take profits," said Bunsom Kesapradist of Asia Credit.
Finance and bank counters lost 2.72 and 1.57 percent respectively.
Investors sold large banks and finance firms after their strong rallies earlier this week, Bunsom said.
Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, falling one baht to 55.50, Thai Military Bank slipped two to 55, National Finance dropped 1.50 to 47.50, and TelecomAsia rose two to 52.
Brokers said the market is expected to get support and resistance at 830 and 850 respectively on Monday.
